## School E-Waste Recycling in Kochi
URL: https://www.ewastekochi.com/school-e-waste-recycling/
Description: School e-waste recycling in Kochi — computer lab retirement, office IT clearance, projector and printer disposal for schools, colleges and educational campuses.
Headings: School E-Waste Recycling in Kochi | Quick answer | What we accept | How the process works | Why school pickup timing matters | Computer lab refresh vs mixed clearance | Documentation typical schools request | Frequently asked questions | Frequently Asked Questions | Related pages

Schools, colleges and educational campuses have a distinct e-waste profile — computer labs with 30-100 near-identical desktops, admin offices with a small IT fleet, projectors and interactive whiteboards from classrooms, printers and copiers from staff rooms. This page covers how educational e-waste is scheduled around term calendars, what documentation schools typically need, and how a computer lab refresh differs from a mixed clearance.
For school e-waste recycling in Kochi, WhatsApp Ewaste Kochi with the campus location, an approximate inventory (computer lab count, admin devices, projectors, printers), and preferred scheduling window (vacations usually work best). The team confirms a scheduled pickup and produces the documentation your finance office typically needs. Pickup is free for eligible collections; per-device tracking and data destruction are optional add-ons quoted before the job.
Educational campuses have unusual scheduling constraints. Term-time pickup is disruptive — computer labs, staff rooms, and admin offices are all in active use, students and staff are on campus, and moving equipment through corridors affects the school day. Vacation pickup — summer break, mid-term breaks, annual holidays — is much easier for everyone.
Most educational bookings coordinate around the school calendar: computer lab refresh is planned for the long summer break, mixed office clearance is planned for shorter mid-term breaks, and admin-only pickups (single laptop replacement, printer retirement) can slot into normal working days without much disruption.
Give 2-3 weeks notice for pickups tied to vacation windows — the specific slots fill up quickly, and access coordination with the school's estate/facility team takes time.
Two common scenarios drive most school bookings:
Computer lab refresh — 30 to 100 similar desktops being replaced with a new batch. Straightforward from an inventory perspective (largely uniform), but logistically substantial. Typically routes through ITAD workflow with per-machine serial capture (useful for the school's asset register update). Buyback check for viable units; recycling for the rest. Certificate of Destruction for the shared-drive lab machines if they held student data.
Mixed office clearance — a heterogeneous batch: an old projector from a seminar hall, a broken printer from the staff room, three retired laptops from the admin office, some UPS batteries from the server room. Routes through standard bulk pickup — no per-serial capture needed unless the school specifically wants it. Single visit usually sufficient.
School finance and administration offices usually need more paperwork than a consumer pickup for compliance, audit, and asset-register purposes:
GST invoice — for schools that need the pickup on the books for accounting.
Per-device asset log — for updating the school's asset register when specific machines are retired. Shows serial, model, condition, and disposition per device.
Certificate of Destruction — for any admin machines that held student records, staff records, financial data, or exam papers. Serialised per drive for high-sensitivity data.
Annual disposal record — for finance audit trails, showing the categories, counts, and disposition of e-waste retired during the financial year.
For grants, CSR reports, or ESG filings some campuses need — the environmental disposal record can be issued in the requested format.
Yes — a common booking. 30 to 100 similar desktops in one visit (or multi-day for very large labs), with per-machine serial capture for the school's asset register and Certificates of Destruction for the shared-drive machines. Typically scheduled around vacation windows.

'Computer' covers a lot when it comes to buyback — desktops, laptops, all-in-ones, workstations, servers. All can potentially qualify for a quote depending on model, age and condition. This page covers what generally qualifies, how the process works for each type, and when a computer is worth more sold than recycled.
To sell an old computer in Kochi, WhatsApp Ewaste Kochi with the type (desktop, laptop, workstation, server), brand, model, specs and photos. A condition-based estimate is returned; the team picks up at the confirmed slot, inspects, and pays on the spot for accepted quotes. Non-viable computers route to free recycling instead — no obligation to accept a lower confirmed quote.
Not all computers qualify. Rough guide:
Almost always qualify: recent MacBooks (last 3-4 years), recent workstations with meaningful GPU/CPU specs, recent gaming laptops with discrete graphics, business laptops from the last 3 years.
Sometimes qualify: consumer laptops from the last 3-4 years (depends on brand and specs), desktop towers with recent CPU/GPU, all-in-ones from the last 3 years, enterprise servers with current-generation CPUs.
Rarely qualify: consumer desktops 5 years old or older, business machines 6 years old or older, older MacBooks (7 years old or older), machines with heavy visible wear or non-working components.
Don't qualify: non-working machines, physically broken machines, machines with major cosmetic damage, obsolete-generation hardware.
Workstation-class machines — Dell Precision, HP Z, ThinkPad P — often retain value longer than consumer machines because they have a specific enterprise buyer market. Same for gaming laptops with discrete GPUs (RTX cards especially) and video-editing workstations with high-end CPU/GPU/RAM configurations.
Enterprise servers are more niche. Buyback exists but the market is narrower and quotes vary widely by generation. Send full model info (Dell PowerEdge Rxxx, HPE ProLiant DLxxx, Cisco UCS Cxxx) plus CPU generation and RAM for the specific estimate.
Rough rule of thumb: if the machine is under 5 years old, works, and was reasonably specced when new, get a buyback estimate before assuming it's recycling-only. Estimates are free and non-committal.
If the machine is over 8-10 years old or doesn't work, it's almost certainly recycling. That's not a bad outcome — free pickup and proper material recovery is still worth doing.

The number is based on second-hand market data for that specific model plus condition adjustments. Five variables move it:
Brand — Apple retains value best; ThinkPad, Dell business, HP EliteBook next; consumer brands lower; no-brand laptops usually recycling only.
Model + year — a 2022 XPS 13 is not the same product as a 2015 XPS 13. Year matters significantly for the resale market.
Condition — powers on cleanly, screen intact, keys working, casing OK, battery holds reasonable charge.
Drive — laptop with SSD/HDD included is worth more than one without.
Cosmetics — dents, scratches, worn keyboard, faded screen all reduce the number.
Every quote before physical inspection is an estimate, labelled that way in the message. Physical inspection almost always reveals something the photos didn't:
Keys that stick, a battery that drains in an hour, a hinge that grinds, a subtle screen defect, a fan that never quiets down — small things that materially affect resale value.
Sometimes inspection reveals better condition than the photos suggested — the quote goes up.
If the confirmed quote comes in lower than the estimate and you'd rather not sell at that number, you can decline. The team doesn't collect the laptop, no pickup fee, no restocking fee, no consequence. The laptop stays with you.

## Hard Drive Degaussing in Kochi
URL: https://www.ewastekochi.com/services/hard-drive-degaussing-kochi/
Description: Hard drive degaussing in Kochi — magnetic erasure for hard disk drives, distinct from wiping or physical shredding. Certificate available on request.
Headings: Hard Drive Degaussing in Kochi | Quick answer | Degaussing vs. wiping vs. shredding | Important limitation | Process | Who this is for | Frequently Asked Questions

Degaussing uses a strong magnetic field to erase data on magnetic hard
    drives — a distinct method from overwrite-wiping or physical shredding,
    suited to bulk drive retirement where reuse isn't the goal.
Hard drive degaussing in Kochi — magnetic erasure for hard disk drives, distinct from wiping or physical shredding. Certificate available on request.
Wiping (see our main data
      destruction page) overwrites data on a drive that still works, so
      it can be reused or resold afterward. Degaussing scrambles data magnetically — fast for
      bulk volumes of traditional hard disk drives, but the drive can't be
      reused afterward since its magnetic formatting is destroyed too. Physical shredding (see
hard drive shredding) mechanically
      destroys the drive — used for damaged drives or where policy requires
      physical destruction regardless of condition.
Degaussing only works on magnetic media — traditional hard disk
      drives. It does not work on SSDs, which don't store data magnetically
      and need wiping or physical destruction instead. Tell us your drive
      types when you schedule so the right method is used.
Businesses retiring bulk quantities of traditional hard drives where
      reuse isn't needed, and anyone who wants a fast, thorough erasure
      method for magnetic media specifically. For SSDs or mixed
      drive types, ask us about combining degaussing with wiping or
      shredding as appropriate.
മലയാളത്തിൽ സഹായം വേണോ? ഞങ്ങളെ +91 75005 55454 എന്ന നമ്പറിൽ വിളിക്കുകയോ വാട്സ്ആപ്പ് ചെയ്യുകയോ ചെയ്യാം.
Wiping overwrites data on a drive that still works, so it can be reused. Degaussing uses a strong magnetic field to scramble the data on magnetic media, rendering the drive unusable afterward but not physically destroyed. Shredding physically destroys the drive. Each suits a different situation — see below.
No — degaussing only works on magnetic storage media (traditional hard disk drives). SSDs need wiping or physical destruction instead, since they don't store data magnetically.
No, degaussing renders the drive's magnetic formatting unusable, so it can't be reused for storage — it's a one-way process suited to drives you're retiring, not reselling.
Degaussing is faster for bulk magnetic drive volumes and still renders data unrecoverable. Shredding is preferred when physical destruction is specifically required by policy, or the drive is damaged. Ask us if you're unsure which fits your situation.

## Where to Recycle Tablets in Kochi
URL: https://www.ewastekochi.com/tablet-recycling/
Description: Where to recycle old tablets in Kochi — iPads and Android tablets, working or damaged. Free doorstep pickup, condition-based buyback quote, data destruction.
Headings: Where to Recycle Tablets in Kochi | Quick answer | What we accept | How the process works | Why iPad Activation Lock and Android FRP matter for buyback | Accessories — Apple Pencil, keyboards, cases | Damaged tablets — cracked screens, dead batteries | Frequently asked questions | Frequently Asked Questions | Related pages

Tablets fall between phones and laptops in the buyback market — iPads retain meaningful value longer than most Android tablets, but the second-hand tablet market is real. This page covers what tablets qualify for buyback, why factory-resetting matters (especially for iPads with Activation Lock), and how damaged or dead tablets get handled.
To recycle a tablet in Kochi, WhatsApp Ewaste Kochi with the brand, model, storage size, condition and photos. Working iPads and recent Android tablets usually qualify for a condition-based buyback quote. Factory-reset before pickup (iPad: sign out of Apple ID; Android: remove Google account). Damaged or dead tablets route to free recycling with data destruction.
Every iPad from 2013 onward has Activation Lock tied to the original owner's Apple ID. If the tablet still has Activation Lock enabled when handed over, no one can set it up — the buyer effectively receives a paperweight. Same for Android tablets since roughly 2015 with Factory Reset Protection (FRP): removing the Google account after reset unlocks the device for the next owner.
For buyback to work: factory reset first, sign out of the account, then hand over. The team verifies the tablet reaches the setup screen unlocked before confirming the buyback quote.
If you can't reset (forgotten Apple ID password, locked out of Google account, device won't power on), flag it when booking. The tablet routes through data destruction instead of buyback — no buyback payment, but pickup is still free and the storage is properly destroyed.
iPad accessories often have meaningful independent value. Apple Pencil (both generations), Magic Keyboard, Smart Keyboard Folio, first-party Smart Covers all retain some resale value.
Include accessories in the pickup — either they add to the buyback quote (for the working iPad + accessories bundle) or they get their own smaller quote if the iPad itself doesn't qualify. Third-party keyboards and cases usually don't have meaningful buyback value but are still accepted for recycling.
Cracked-screen tablets: often still qualify for reduced buyback if the tablet works despite the crack. Touch input failing (partial dead zones, ghost touches) reduces the quote significantly.
Dead battery: swelling is a real risk with older iPads and Android tablets kept in hot conditions. If the battery is swelling (screen popping out of the frame, casing curved), flag it and photograph — battery pickup goes through separate safe-transport handling.
Water-damaged: usually no buyback (internal corrosion unpredictable). Route: recycling with data destruction — assume storage may still be technically recoverable.
Depends on model, storage size, cellular/WiFi variant, and condition. Recent iPads (last 3-4 years) usually get meaningful quotes; iPad Pro retains more value than base iPad or iPad Mini. Send About screen + photos for a specific number.
Yes. Recent Samsung Galaxy Tab (S-series especially) qualifies. Mid-range Android tablets get reduced quotes. Very old or low-end tablets usually go to recycling only.
If it still works, reduced buyback quote is possible. If touch input is failing or the crack has made the tablet unusable, recycling only. Photo of the damage helps the estimate.
Yes for buyback — factory reset + sign out of Apple ID clears Activation Lock. If you can't (forgotten Apple ID password, device won't power on), flag it — the tablet routes through data destruction instead of buyback.
Include them in the pickup. First-party accessories (Apple Pencil, Magic Keyboard, Smart Keyboard) have their own resale value — either bundled into the iPad quote or separately quoted.

## UPS Recycling in Kochi
URL: https://www.ewastekochi.com/ups-recycling/
Description: UPS recycling in Kochi — home and office UPS units, single and battery-bank installations. Safe battery separation, material recovery for the electronics.
Headings: UPS Recycling in Kochi | Quick answer | What we accept | How the process works | Why battery separation matters for UPS recycling | Bulk UPS retirement — server rooms and telecom | When UPS units might qualify for buyback | Frequently asked questions | Frequently Asked Questions | Related pages

UPS units — the battery-backed power supplies protecting computers, servers, network cabinets and home electronics from power fluctuations — retire on a steady cycle because internal batteries wear out every 3-5 years. This page covers what UPS types get accepted, why battery separation matters, and how bulk UPS retirement (server rooms, offices with battery banks) is planned.
To recycle a UPS unit in Kochi, WhatsApp Ewaste Kochi with the type (home / office small / rack-mount / battery bank), rough count and your location. Batteries are separated at pickup for lead-acid recycling; the electronics of the UPS route to material recovery. Doorstep pickup is free for eligible collections; large battery banks may need scheduled transport.
The UPS chassis (electronics, transformer, chassis metal) and the internal batteries (typically sealed lead-acid) route to completely different recycling streams. Lead-acid batteries have a well-established recycling infrastructure in India — lead is recovered for reuse in new batteries; acid is neutralised. UPS electronics route to standard e-waste material recovery.
For safe transport, batteries are separated from the UPS chassis at pickup (or at the facility, depending on the UPS size). This is why UPS units aren't just 'thrown in' with general e-waste — the separate-stream handling starts at the pickup itself.
Offices, telecom sites, apartment building generator-rooms, and small data centres retire full battery banks at once — 4, 8, 20, or more heavy lead-acid units at a time. Bulk battery pickup is a scheduling and transport problem different from single UPS pickup:
Weight — a 100Ah SLA battery weighs ~30 kg. A bank of 8 is 240 kg. Bulk pickup needs proper vehicle capacity, load securing, and lifting equipment.
Chain of custody — some sites have formal documentation requirements for battery disposal (particularly telecom, data centre, healthcare). Per-battery serial logging available under ITAD workflow.
Scheduling — advance planning (3-5 working days minimum) so transport is lined up. Very large jobs may need multiple pickup visits.
Working, recent (last 2 years) UPS units in good condition may occasionally qualify for reduced buyback — the buyback market for UPS is smaller than for laptops or phones, but it exists. Enterprise-grade rack-mount UPS (APC, Eaton, Emerson) is more likely to have resale value than consumer-grade home UPS.
For most UPS retirement scenarios, though, the internal battery has degraded to the point where the unit doesn't hold charge — which is why it's being retired in the first place. Free pickup + battery separation + material recovery is the typical route.
Message Ewaste Kochi with UPS type, count, and your location. Doorstep pickup is arranged based on area. Batteries are separated at pickup for lead-acid recycling; the electronics route to material recovery.
Yes. UPS batteries can be recycled separately if you've already removed them from the chassis. Flag battery specs (voltage, capacity, count) in your message. Lead-acid batteries route to established recycling with lead recovery.
Flag it when booking and include a photo. Leaking or swollen batteries need appropriate containment for safe transport. Do not attempt to puncture, crush, or manually drain a leaking battery yourself.
Rack-mount UPS removal usually coordinated with your IT team (rack removal, disconnection). Ewaste Kochi collects the removed units. Battery banks need dedicated transport — 3-5 working days notice typical.
Yes — same lead-acid recycling stream as UPS batteries. Inverter units (the electronics) recycle separately. See also /battery-recycling/ for the broader battery flow.
